name: Binance
one_liner: Binance is a cryptocurrency exchange offering spot, margin, futures, and wallet trading via a large REST API.
needs_human_reasons: only 0% of quotes grounded in cited pages

evidence.quote: Signatures generated using HMAC are not case-sensitive.
It is highly recommended to use Ed25519 API keys
Secure endpoints require a valid API key to be specified and authenticated.
before creating an API Key, you need to make a deposit of any amount to your Spot Wallet to activate your account and complete identity verification
API keys can be created on the API Management page of your Binance account.

notes: Docs moved from binance-docs.github.io to developers.binance.com (github.io now redirects). REST API is free self-serve via the Binance account's API Management page, but creating a key requires 2FA, a Spot Wallet deposit, and identity (KYC) verification first — a real-world friction point beyond typical dev-account signup, hence yellow rather than green. Auth is a static API key sent via X-MBX-APIKEY header plus a request signature (HMAC, RSA, or Ed25519) — not OAuth2/JWT/bearer/basic. API surface is very large (spot, margin, futures, options, wallet, sub-account endpoints combined run into the hundreds). No vendor-published MCP server found; several community MCP servers exist on GitHub and in the MCP registry (all community-maintained, none official).
